correctness.rationale: Starting from the radial backward equation, independent differentiation verifies the kernel h_nu and normalization sqrt(2D). For nu>=1 the monotone integral in w proves strict decreasing dependence on D; for nu=1/2 the differential identity plus a one-crossing comparison with z/(z-1/2) proves one unique kernel maximum and hence one unique mean-exit-time optimum. The planar exponential-integral formula and its Laplace endpoint asymptotic are exact, and the small/large noise limits agree with the normalized generator. A separate executable numerical crosscheck is included; finite tests are not substituted for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: For a canonical unstable linear diffusion and the same spherical exit geometry used in the 2026 stochastic-inertia example, the prior local derivative cannot determine whether the noise-induced delay persists or has one/many optima. The theorem resolves the entire nonperturbative noise range for every integer spatial dimension, proves uniqueness and calibrates the physical optimum in dimension one, and identifies a critical two-dimensional exponentially small exit-time effect invisible at every algebraic order. These are motivated structural distinctions, not arbitrary numerical parameter slices.
